title: Business Logic & Problem Solving
goal: Translate business requirements into clear, testable algorithms.

topics.title: Requirement decomposition
topics.description: Break a request into inputs, outputs, rules, and observable outcomes.
learningGoals: Break a request into inputs, outputs, rules, and observable outcomes.
Explain the tradeoffs and demonstrate one failure or boundary case.
examples: Apply requirement decomposition to a session, coupon, or token lifecycle. Compare a successful operation with one that must be rejected.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

topics.title: Preconditions
topics.description: State what must be true before an operation can begin.
learningGoals: State what must be true before an operation can begin.
Explain Input validity, Required state and Rejection.
Demonstrate a valid operation and a boundary or failure case.
examples: Before cancellation, require an existing order in a cancellable state. Specify the error for each rejected state.

tasks.title: Explain Preconditions in your own words
Work through the example and predict the result
Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help

topics.title: Postconditions
topics.description: State what must be true after success and after failure.
learningGoals: State what must be true after success and after failure.
Explain Success outcome, Failure outcome and Observable state.
Demonstrate a valid operation and a boundary or failure case.
examples: After a successful refund, the total refunded amount increases once. After a rejected refund, no money state changes.

tasks.title: Explain Postconditions in your own words
Work through the example and predict the result
Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help

topics.title: Invariants
topics.description: Identify rules that must remain true through every state change.
learningGoals: Identify rules that must remain true through every state change.
Explain Always-valid rules, Atomic changes and State consistency.
Demonstrate a valid operation and a boundary or failure case.
examples: The sum of refunds must never exceed the paid amount, even when two refund requests arrive concurrently.

Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help
